stem: What is the name of Megasthenes’ book?
expl: Chandragupta Maurya was a contemporary of Alexander. Foreign writers contemporary to Alexander include Nearchus, Onesicritus, Aristobulus, and Megasthenes, whose accounts provide information about Chandragupta Maurya. Among these foreign writers, Megasthenes is the most important, and his book “Indica” is a major source for Mauryan history. In “Indica”, Megasthenes describes the municipal administration of Pataliputra. According to him, the administration of the city was carried out through committees comprising a total of 30 members. There were 6 committees in all, and each committee had 5 members. One committee was responsible for collecting sales tax. Sales tax was collected as one-tenth of the value. Those who evaded taxes were awarded the death penalty.

stem: What is the name of Kalhana’s book?
expl: Kalhana wrote the history of Kashmir in Rajatarangini. He composed this work during the reign of Jayasimha (1128– 1149 AD). Chanakya (Kautilya), the Prime Minister of Chandragupta Maurya, wrote the famous treatise Arthashastra on political science.

stem: Kautilya's Arthashastra is a book based on -

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Arthashastra, written by Kautilya (Chanakya) during the Mauryan period, is a book on the principles and practice of governance. It explains the Mandala theory of the state, which discusses foreign policy. It also describes the Saptanga theory—Swami, Amatya, Janapada, Durga, Kosha, Danda, and Mitra. The Arthashastra also gives detailed information about the administration of that time, as well as agriculture, crafts, and trade.

stem: ‘Kumarasambhava,’ an epic poem was composed by –
expl: The epic Kumarasambhavam was composed by the great poet Kalidasa. It has 17 cantos (only the first eight cantos were written by Kalidasa; the remaining nine cantos were written by other poets). It contains vivid description of nature and narrates the birth of Kartikeya and the slaying of Tarakasura.

stem: Who wrote the book 'Harshacharita'?
expl: Harshacharita was written by the famous author Banabhatta. It is a major source for the history of the Vardhana dynasty. It is an akhyayika (a biographical narrative) in which the author presents the life of his contemporary ruler and the ruler’s ancestors.

stem: Nitisara, an early book of politics, was written by
expl: Nitisara, composed by Kamandaka, is an important collection of 1,192 verses (shlokas). It is arranged into 34 sections (prakaranas) and 20 chapters or cantos (sargas). It includes the traditional branches of learning: the state, its constituents and protection, the Mandala theory of inter-state relations, various kinds of policies, war and peace, diplomacy and wisdom, military organization, and the faults that should be avoided. The appendix lists, for comparison, the contents of Kautilya’s Arthashastra and Kamandaka’s Nitisara.
